coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 54
record.distance_note: On Terry A. Francois Blvd, within the stretch DataSF's official 'Former San Francisco Redevelopment Agency Project Areas' boundary marks as Mission Bay South, and about 30m from Mission Bay South's own nearest tracked feature (the UCSF Illinois Street Garage/P24 waterfront lawn) -- versus roughly 470m from Mission Rock's own tracked footprint (Pier 48/50). Recorded as adjacent to Mission Bay, not Mission Rock, on that basis. Pier 54 itself predates and is not part of Mission Bay's OCII development program -- it is Port-jurisdiction maritime infrastructure.

record.summary: Pier 54, a Port-owned pier on Terry A. Francois Blvd, was condemned and closed in 2024 after years of structural deterioration, displacing the businesses that operated there. The Port's draft Five-Year Capital Improvement Program (FY2027-31) budgets $2.0M to demolish the pier's shed; no funded timeline exists yet for removing the rest of the structure.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- a coarse placeholder box, not a traced footprint, for the same reasons as the Pier 70 dry docks shape (no parcel, no source figure). The box does not represent the real pier structure's true shape or its full extent into the Bay.
notes.digitized_from: No Assessor block/lot exists for this Port pier structure (confirmed: DataSF's 'Parcels - Active and Retired' dataset, acdm-wktn, has no parcels with PIER-numbered street names). No Port GIS shapefile or site-plan figure was available, so this is a coarse locational box centered on the real DataSF street-centerline address range 500-599 Terry A. Francois Blvd, the address range covering the Pier 52/54 area (California State Parks Division of Boating and Waterways lists a combined 'Pier 54 & Pier 52 BLF' boat-launch facility on Terry A. Francois Blvd in this same stretch).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Port pier structure; not on the Assessor's secured roll (data.sf.gov acdm-wktn has no PIER-numbered parcels near this site).
notes.regulatory_context: Condemned and red-tagged in 2024; the Port announced it would permanently close at the end of 2024, displacing the pier's tenant businesses (SFGate, Sept 2024). The Port's draft Five-Year Capital Improvement Program (FY2027-31, Feb 2026) budgets a 'Pier 54 Shed Demolition' line item totaling $2.0M ($500,000 in FY2026-27 and $1,500,000 in FY2027-28); no line item for full substructure removal appears in that document.

open_questions: No funded plan yet for removing the pier's substructure beyond the shed demolition.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the closure-announcement milestone was dated December 2024, but the Port's August 9, 2024 memo says formal written notice went to tenants on July 15, 2024 and SFGate reported the closure in September 2024; it is now dated July 15, 2024. The February 2026 draft CIP milestone was flagged expected although the draft was published then; the flag was removed. Whether the shed demolition has started, and so whether 'being removed' is the right map status, is for the owner to confirm: no source read says it has.

That the Port planned to fence the pier to prevent vandalism is reported only in a search-engine summary of the SFGate article, not independently re-verified here against the full original article text (which sits behind a paywall; the mirror used for this record's other facts may not repeat that detail).

This record's site grouping ("Mission Bay South") reflects DataSF's official redevelopment-project-area boundary, which reaches this stretch of Terry A. Francois Blvd -- not a claim that Pier 54 is a Mission Bay OCII development block, which it is not.

record.notes: This is a Port maritime/pier facility, not an OCII Mission Bay South development block -- grouped under the Mission Bay South site here because that is the nearest tracked site and because DataSF's official 'Former San Francisco Redevelopment Agency Project Areas' boundary for Mission Bay South extends north along the Terry A. Francois Blvd shoreline to include this stretch. It is materially farther from Mission Rock's own tracked footprint (Pier 48/50, ~470m away) than from Mission Bay South's nearest tracked features (the UCSF Illinois Street Garage/P24 lawn, ~30m away). Recorded as adjacent rather than tracked because it is Port-jurisdiction maritime infrastructure being demolished, not a Mission Bay OCII development parcel like this site's other tracked records.
